bugs.name: Uploaded workspace picture disappears after the first refresh
bugs.summary: A valid workspace picture appears immediately after upload, but the first settled refresh of General settings can show an empty picture and disable Remove.
bugs.expected: A successfully uploaded workspace picture remains visible and removable after refreshing General settings.
bugs.actual: The picture appears after upload, then the first settled refresh shows the empty picture placeholder with Remove disabled. The uploaded file remains stored, and a later refresh may restore its display.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > General with no workspace picture set.
Upload a valid square PNG or JPEG under 10 MB and confirm the picture appears with Remove enabled.
Refresh General settings and wait for the page to finish loading.
Observe the empty picture placeholder and disabled Remove control.

bugs.name: Regenerating an API key shortens its saved expiration
bugs.summary: Immediately regenerating an API key with a finite expiration repeatedly shortens its saved lifetime by roughly one additional day each time.
bugs.expected: Regenerating an API key renews its configured expiration duration without cumulatively losing days.
bugs.actual: Each immediate regeneration moves the persisted expiration earlier by roughly another day. The shortened expiration survives reloading, while reloading without regeneration preserves it.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > MCP & APIs > API.
Create a disposable API key with a unique name, an available role, and a 15-day expiration. Save it and note its expiration.
Reload the key details, select Regenerate Key, enter yes, and confirm.
Reload the details and observe the shortened remaining lifetime.
Immediately regenerate the key again and reload. Observe another roughly one-day reduction rather than renewal of the original duration.

bugs.name: Clearing a saved AI skill description does not persist
bugs.summary: Clearing an existing AI skill description appears to work, but reopening or refreshing the skill restores the previous description.
bugs.expected: Removing an optional skill description persists after autosave, just like replacing it with another nonempty description.
bugs.actual: An empty or whitespace-only description is silently discarded. After waiting for autosave and reopening or refreshing the skill, the previous description returns; nonempty changes persist.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > AI > Skills and create a disposable skill with a unique name, nonempty description, and instructions. Save it.
Reopen the skill, clear its description completely, blur the field, and wait at least three seconds for autosave.
Return to the skills list and reopen the skill, or refresh its editor.
Observe that the previous description returns. Replacing the description with different nonempty text persists under the same steps.

bugs.name: Restricted members see an unusable Invite user action that silently redirects to Profile
bugs.summary: The workspace menu offers Invite user to members without invitation permission, but selecting it silently redirects to Profile instead of explaining that the action is unavailable.
bugs.expected: An invitation action unavailable to the current member is hidden or disabled, or explains the permission restriction when selected.
bugs.actual: Invite user appears as an available workspace-menu action for a restricted member. Selecting it closes the menu and leaves the member on Profile with no invitation form or permission explanation. Authorized administrators can still use the invitation flow.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace member who lacks permission to manage workspace members, and open Settings > Profile.
Open the navigation sidebar if it is collapsed, then open the workspace dropdown.
Select Invite user.
Observe that the dropdown closes and Profile is displayed without an invitation form or permission explanation.

bugs.name: Mouse clicks on navigation folder contents fail in a fresh narrow-width session
bugs.summary: At a narrow browser width, ordinary mouse clicks on saved navigation folder contents fail to open their destinations until layout customization has been entered in the current session.
bugs.expected: Clicking a saved navigation item with a mouse opens its configured destination at narrow widths, as it does at desktop widths.
bugs.actual: At a 390-by-844 viewport after reload, mouse clicks on folder contents neither navigate nor open a destination tab, and the folder panel remains open. Touch taps, desktop-width mouse clicks, and narrow-width top-level navigation items work. Entering and canceling layout customization temporarily restores the folder mouse clicks; reloading restores the failure.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator at desktop width, open Settings > Layout > Customize. Create and save a disposable navigation folder containing a custom link to the current application origin plus /settings/layout.
Confirm that clicking the saved link at desktop width opens Layout settings.
Resize the browser viewport to 390 by 844 pixels and reload. Do not enter layout customization after this reload.
Open workspace navigation, open the saved folder, and click its nested link with an ordinary stationary mouse click.
Observe that no destination opens and the folder panel remains visible. Repeat the click to confirm the failure.
Enter layout customization and cancel it, then retry the same folder link with the mouse. Observe that it now works; reload and repeat the narrow-width click to observe the failure again.

bugs.name: Reactivating a custom field does not restore its record layout placement
bugs.summary: After a displayed custom field is deactivated and reactivated, it is active in Data model settings but remains absent from saved record Fields layouts.
bugs.expected: Reactivating a previously displayed custom field restores its placement in the record Fields section, including access to its existing value.
bugs.actual: The reactivated field is listed as active in settings but remains missing from the record Fields section and side panel after reload, while other visible fields remain. Manually adding the field back through Edit Layout restores it with its saved value, so the data has not been deleted.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom object with a Multi-select field containing a Red option and another field to use as an unchanged control.
Create a record, set the Multi-select field to Red, and use a saved record Fields layout in which both the Multi-select and control fields are visible.
Deactivate the Multi-select field in Data model settings and confirm it disappears from the record while the control field remains visible.
Reopen the field settings and activate it again. Confirm it appears as active in the settings field list.
Reload the record page and reopen its side panel. Observe that the reactivated field remains absent from the Fields section.
Use Edit Layout to show the field again. Observe that the Red value returns and remains after reload.

bugs.name: Select option API-value collisions disable Save without explaining the error
bugs.summary: Select option labels that generate the same API value disable Save without showing the collision error, even when the visible labels differ.
bugs.expected: The field editor displays a validation error explaining the API-value collision while blocking the invalid save.
bugs.actual: Renaming an option to Ready! while another option is Ready generates the same internal value READY for both. Save becomes disabled without displaying the duplicate-value error. With Advanced settings off, the conflicting API values are hidden. Correcting the collision enables Save.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom Select field with Draft and Ready options, and save it.
Reopen the field editor with Advanced settings off and rename Draft to Ready!.
Blur the option input. Observe that the distinct visible labels Ready! and Ready leave Save disabled without an explanation of the conflicting internal values.
Rename the changed option to a distinct value such as Done. Observe that Save becomes enabled and the valid options can be saved.

bugs.name: Roles-only permission allows role editing but cannot reach the Roles list
bugs.summary: A user granted Roles permission without Users permission can edit roles directly, but the Roles breadcrumb redirects to Profile and role-list navigation is absent.
bugs.expected: A user permitted to manage roles can reach the Roles list and return to it from an allowed role editor without also needing permission to add or remove users.
bugs.actual: The role editor is accessible and role edits save, but its Roles breadcrumb and the Roles list route redirect to Profile. Members and Roles entries are absent from the settings sidebar. Enabling Users in addition to Roles restores the list and navigation; disabling Users restores the failure.
reproSteps: As an administrator, create a disposable role with Settings All Access off, Roles on, and Users plus other individual settings permissions off. Record an existing role editor link.
Assign the role to a secondary workspace member, then sign in as that member with the updated permissions.
Observe that the settings sidebar has no Members or Roles entry.
Open the recorded role editor link and confirm that the role editor is available and a description edit can be saved and retained after reload.
Click the Roles breadcrumb and observe that Profile opens instead of the Roles list.
As the administrator, enable only Users in addition to Roles for the same member role. Reload or sign in again as the member and verify that the Roles breadcrumb now opens the list.

bugs.name: Metadata refetch in another tab discards unsaved data-model forms
bugs.summary: After the data model changes in a separate authenticated session, loading the app in another tab of the original session can reset its open valid field form and discard unsaved settings.
bugs.expected: Background metadata synchronization preserves valid unsaved field settings in an unchanged foreground tab.
bugs.actual: The foreground relation form loses its source name, inverse name and destination; a Text-field form loses its name. Save becomes disabled. Persisted records or saved settings are not deleted.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and create disposable source and target objects.
In browser session A, start a new relation field on the source, select the target and enter unique source and inverse names; leave this valid draft unsaved.
In an independently authenticated browser session B, create a new Text field on the target through Settings > Data model. Leave session A open and confirm its draft remains.
Open another tab in browser session A and load a normal app page, such as Companies, while keeping the original field form open.

Observe that the original tab can briefly show a loader, then return to an empty form with the source and inverse names cleared, default destination, and disabled Save. Repeat with a fresh relation or Text-field draft.

bugs.name: Abbreviated Opportunity amounts ignore comma-decimal number preferences
bugs.summary: Saved comma-decimal number preferences are ignored by abbreviated currency amounts and aggregate summaries in Opportunities.
bugs.expected: Abbreviated amounts and aggregate summaries use the saved number-format preference, including a comma decimal separator when Dots and comma is selected.
bugs.actual: After selecting Dots and comma, short amounts and summaries retain decimal points, such as $2.5m and Average 1.3m, instead of comma-decimal formatting. Full-format currency displays follow the same preference correctly; the preference remains saved.
reproSteps: Use Opportunity records with fractional abbreviated amounts, such as 2,500,000 and 123,500, displayed using short currency formatting.
Open Settings > Experience and set Number format to Dots and comma, with example 1.234,56. Confirm the saved preference.
Open Opportunities and inspect the abbreviated Amount values and an Average or Sum summary containing a fractional abbreviated value.
Observe decimal points in the short amounts and summary rather than the selected decimal commas.
As a control, inspect a Full-format currency field containing the same amount and confirm that it follows the comma-decimal preference.

bugs.name: Data-model diagram object titles open the generic catalog instead of object details
bugs.summary: Clicking a named object title in the data-model visualizer opens the overall object catalog instead of that object’s data-model details.
bugs.expected: Selecting an object title in the data-model visualizer opens the selected object’s data-model details, as the normal object catalog does.
bugs.actual: Companies, Dashboards, and a fresh custom object title each open the generic Data model catalog at /settings/objects. Selecting the same object from the catalog opens its correct details. The catalog remains usable as a workaround; no data is lost.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Data model and select Visualize data model.
Click an unobscured object title such as Companies. If another card covers it, drag the covering card away first.
Observe that the generic object catalog opens instead of the selected object’s details.
Return to the diagram and repeat with another named object or a fresh custom object. Observe the same generic catalog destination.
As a control, select that object from the normal Data model catalog and confirm that its object-specific details open.

bugs.name: Role Assignment shows a far-future date for Never expires API keys
bugs.summary: An API key configured to Never expires is displayed with a far-future calendar expiry in its role Assignment table.
bugs.expected: The role Assignment expiry summary displays Never expires for the same keys that the API key details and inventory identify as never expiring.
bugs.actual: API key details show Never expires and the API key inventory shows Never, but the role’s Assigned API keys table renders a far-future calendar date in Expires, including after reload. This is a display inconsistency; no actual key-use failure or expiry loss was observed.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable role that is assignable to API keys.
Create a disposable API key with expiration set to Never and assign it to that role, either during creation or through the role Assignment tab.
Open the API key details and confirm the expiration is shown as Never expires.
Open the role’s Assignment tab and locate the key under Assigned API keys.
Inspect Expires and reload. Observe a far-future calendar date rather than Never expires while the key details retain Never expires.

bugs.name: Profile picture preview stays blank after a valid replacement following an invalid upload
bugs.summary: After an unsupported upload breaks the profile picture preview, a subsequent valid image saves successfully but the preview stays gray until reload or remount.
bugs.expected: Uploading a valid replacement image refreshes the profile picture preview immediately, including after an earlier image failed to render.
bugs.actual: Following a plain-text picture upload, later valid PNG uploads leave the picture tile as a gray placeholder after the upload settles. Reloading the page or leaving Profile and returning displays the newly saved valid image. Valid-image-to-valid-image replacement works without a prior broken preview; no saved image is lost.
reproSteps: At a 390-by-844 viewport, open Settings > Profile and upload a valid square PNG under 10 MB. Confirm it appears.
Upload a small plain-text .txt file through the same picture control and observe the broken or gray placeholder preview.
Upload a different valid square PNG and wait for the upload to settle.
Observe that the preview remains gray instead of showing the valid replacement.
Reload the page, or leave Profile and return. Confirm that the new valid picture appears, demonstrating that it was saved.

bugs.name: Navigation layout saves malformed link URLs that open a browser error page
bugs.summary: The layout editor accepts a URL containing spaces and no valid hostname, publishing an unusable workspace navigation link.
bugs.expected: Saving a navigation link rejects malformed URLs and explains how to correct the value.
bugs.actual: Saving this is not a url succeeds without validation and stores https://this is not a url. The malformed link survives reload and opens a browser error tab when clicked. Valid URL controls save and open successfully through the same flow.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > Layout > Customize and choose Add menu item > Link.
Enter a disposable label and set the URL to this is not a url.
Blur the URL field, save the link, publish the layout, and reload.
Observe that the saved link retains the malformed destination https://this is not a url without a validation error.
Click the link and observe a browser error tab. As a control, create a link to https://example.org through the same flow and confirm that it opens successfully.

bugs.name: Object API-name edits leave indexes without field labels or field-name search
bugs.summary: After editing an object’s API name, existing indexes lose their field labels and cannot be found by field-name search. New index creation can intermittently cause the same display and search failure.
bugs.expected: Saved indexes retain their field labels and remain searchable by those field names after object API-name edits and index creation.
bugs.actual: Existing BTREE and GIN rows can show blank Fields cells after an object API-name edit. Searching Name returns no matching indexes, while searching BTREE still finds the unlabeled index. New index creation intermittently produces the same blank-label and failed-field-search state. Reload restored the labels and search in observed cases, though some reloads retained the incomplete display. No stored-index loss was observed.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom object, enable Advanced settings, and add a Name BTREE index.
Open the object’s Indexes list and verify that the Name field label appears and searching Name finds its index.
Edit and save the object’s singular API name, disabling label/API-name synchronization if necessary, then return to the Indexes list.
Observe blank Fields labels on existing indexes. Search Name and observe no matching indexes; search BTREE and confirm that the unlabeled row is still present.
Reload and compare the labels and field-name search. Reload can restore the missing metadata, although recovery was not consistent across all attempts.
For the intermittent creation variant, repeat adding a Name index on fresh custom objects and inspect its field label and field-name search immediately after saving.

bugs.name: Data-model diagram initially overlaps object cards and obscures their rows
bugs.summary: The initial data-model visualization overlaps neighboring object cards, obscuring field and relationship rows and their expand controls.
bugs.expected: The initial diagram layout allocates enough space for each full object card so that its labels, fields, relationships, and expand controls remain visible.
bugs.actual: Tall object cards overlap neighboring cards on fresh desktop diagram loads. Lower rows and expand controls are obscured, and Fit view or zoom preserves the overlap. Dragging the covering card away reveals the hidden content. No stored data is lost.
reproSteps: At desktop width, open Settings > Data model and select Visualize data model without dragging any cards.
Inspect neighboring cards with enough fields or relationships to extend below their headers. Observe that another card covers lower rows or expand controls.
Use Fit view or zoom and observe that the overlap remains.
Drag the covering card into empty space and confirm that the previously hidden rows and controls become accessible.

bugs.name: Navigation folder and link editors become empty after a mobile or tablet panel close
bugs.summary: At phone and tablet widths, closing a navigation customization panel leaves subsequent folder and link editors without their editing controls.
bugs.expected: Selecting a saved navigation folder or link displays its editing controls each time the editor is opened, including after another panel has been closed.
bugs.actual: At 390-by-844 and 768-by-1000, the first selection on a fresh page works. After closing a panel and selecting a folder or link again, its editor shows only Select a navigation item to edit and a close control. The folder/link settings are unavailable. Desktop close-and-reopen controls work, and saved navigation items remain intact.
reproSteps: At desktop width, create and save a disposable navigation folder with a nested link in Settings > Layout > Customize.
At a 390-by-844 or 768-by-1000 viewport, open layout customization on a fresh page and select a navigation item. Confirm that the initial editor shows its controls.
Close that panel, then select the saved folder again.
Observe that Edit folder contains only Select a navigation item to edit rather than its editing controls.
Close the panel and select the nested link; observe the same empty Edit link state. Compare with working close-and-reopen controls at desktop width.

bugs.name: Saved multi-destination Belongs to one relation reopens as Has many
bugs.summary: A multi-destination relation saved as Belongs to one reopens with Has many in its editor selector and preview, while the Relations list retains the correct saved type.
bugs.expected: The saved relation editor displays Belongs to one, matching the chosen type, stored relation, and Relations list.
bugs.actual: After saving a Belongs to one relation with two destination objects, the refreshed Relations list says Belongs to one, but reopening the editor shows Has many in both selector and preview. Description saves preserve the stored MANY_TO_ONE relation. Single-destination Belongs to one reopens correctly; no record-linking failure or data loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Create three disposable custom objects in Settings > Data model.
On the source object, add a relation targeting the other two objects and provide the required inverse field name.
Choose Belongs to one and save.
Reload and confirm that the Relations list says Belongs to one.
Open the relation editor and observe Has many in its relation-type selector and preview.
As a control, create a single-destination Belongs to one relation and confirm that its editor retains the correct type.

bugs.name: Address Sub-Fields Reset to default does not save or persist
bugs.summary: Reset to default restores all Address subfields in the preview but the reset is omitted from saving, so reopening or refreshing retains the previously saved custom selection.
bugs.expected: Reset to default followed by Save persists the restored default Address subfield selection, just as manually restoring the same checkboxes does.
bugs.actual: After a saved Address field has four or five selected subfields, Reset to default displays Default and all six in the preview. Clicking the enabled Save button sends no field update and leaves the editor open; refresh returns to the previous custom selection. Reset plus a description edit successfully closes the editor and persists the description, but silently drops the reset. Manually restoring the checkboxes saves all six. No record-address data loss was observed.
reproSteps: Create a disposable Address field in Settings > Data model.
Uncheck one or two Address subfields, save, and reopen to confirm the custom selection persists.
Open Sub-Fields and select Reset to default. Observe Default and all six subfields in the preview.
Click the enabled Save button and wait. Observe that the editor remains open, then refresh and confirm that the old custom selection returns.
For a successful-save variation, reset again, change the description, and click Save. Reopen the field and observe that the description persisted but the subfield reset did not.
As a control, manually check the previously omitted subfields, click Save, and reopen. Confirm that all six subfields persist.

bugs.name: Creating a multi-destination relation shows duplicate rows until refresh
bugs.summary: Saving one multi-destination relation displays multiple identical whole-relation rows until the page is refreshed.
bugs.expected: One newly saved multi-destination relation appears as one row representing all its destinations, immediately after Save as well as after refresh.
bugs.actual: A single Save for a relation with two destination objects produces two identical rows in the Relations list. Refresh collapses them to one. A three-destination variation produces three rows then one. Single-destination controls stay at one row. The duplicate rows open working editors; no duplicate stored data, record-linking failure, or data loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Create three disposable custom objects in Settings > Data model.
On the source object, add one relation targeting the other two objects, enter the required inverse field name, and choose Belongs to one.
Click Save once and inspect the Relations list without refreshing.
Observe two identical rows representing that same relation and its two destinations.
Refresh and observe that the rows collapse to one. As a control, create a single-destination relation and confirm that it stays at one row.

bugs.name: Rejected duplicate field rename retargets the editor and later edits or deletion to another field
bugs.summary: After a duplicate field label or API-name rename is rejected, the editor can switch to the conflicting field while retaining the original field URL. Subsequent corrected Save or Delete then affects that other field.
bugs.expected: A rejected duplicate rename leaves the editor and its actions bound to the original field. Correcting or deleting that field must not mutate the unrelated conflicting field.
bugs.actual: When the conflicting field precedes the original in loaded metadata order, the rejected rename leaves the original URL but switches the header or type controls to the conflicting field. A corrected Save renames that other field, and Delete can remove it while preserving the original. Reload clears the switched state. Wrong-field schema mutations were observed; populated-record value loss was not tested.
reproSteps: On a disposable custom object, create a Text field Code and a Rating field Score. The failure is order-dependent: the conflicting field must precede the original field in loaded metadata order.
Open Score, leave label/API-name synchronization enabled, change its label to Code, and click Save.
Observe the duplicate-name error, then inspect the editor: the URL still identifies Score while controls have switched to the existing Text field.
Without reopening the editor, correct the label to a fresh unique name such as Quality and click Save.
Reload the field list and confirm that the original Text Code field became Quality while Rating Score remained unchanged.
On a separate disposable pair showing the same switch, inspect the Delete confirmation and confirm only in test data; the conflicting field is removed while the original remains.

bugs.name: Clearing a Files-based Record image to None reverts after refresh
bugs.summary: A custom object’s Record image setting cannot persist clearing a previously selected Files field to None, even after the automatic update request completes.
bugs.expected: Choosing None clears the custom object’s Record image setting and remains None after the save completes and the settings are reloaded.
bugs.actual: The dropdown shows None and submits an update with a null image identifier. The completed successful response still returns the previous field identifier, and a later metadata read and reload restore that old Files selection. Choosing or switching between non-null Files fields persists correctly. No image-file deletion or record-data loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Create a disposable custom object and a Files field such as Attachments.
In the object Settings tab, select Attachments as Record image and reload to confirm that it persisted.
Choose None. This control submits automatically; observe None in the dropdown.
Allow the update request to finish before refreshing. In the reproduced trial, a three-second wait captured a successful completed response that still returned the old image-field identifier.
Reload the settings and observe that Attachments returns rather than None.
As a control, select a different Files field, wait for the automatic update to complete, and reload to confirm that switching non-null selections persists.

bugs.name: Approved Domains accepts case-only duplicates
bugs.summary: Approved-domain duplicate validation compares domain text case-sensitively, so changing capitalization allows separate saved registrations of the same domain.
bugs.expected: An existing approved domain cannot be registered again by changing only ASCII letter case. The case-equivalent input is normalized or rejected as already registered.
bugs.actual: Repeating the exact lowercase domain is rejected as already registered, but an uppercase or mixed-case equivalent saves successfully. Both variants appear as distinct Pending entries and survive reload. Repeated fresh-domain trials show the same behavior; signup and email-delivery consequences were not tested.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Members > Invite > Add Approved Access Domain.
Register a fresh lowercase domain such as qa-domain.example.test with a valid verification email prefix and save.
Submit the exact same domain again and observe the already-registered error.
Change only the domain’s capitalization, such as QA-DOMAIN.EXAMPLE.TEST, and save.
Reload the Invite page and observe that both case-equivalent domains remain as separate Pending registrations.

bugs.name: Member role selector displays an unrelated role after member applicability is disabled
bugs.summary: Disabling member applicability for an already assigned custom role makes the member’s Permissions role selector display a different role, although the original assignment remains intact.
bugs.expected: The member’s Role selector displays the actual assigned role even when that role is no longer eligible for new member assignments.
bugs.actual: After Assignable to Workspace Members is disabled and saved, the assigned member’s Role selector displays Admin, the first remaining eligible option in the reproduced fixture. Permission checkboxes, Open in Roles, and reassignment confirmation still identify the original custom role. Reload preserves the mismatch, and re-enabling member applicability restores the correct label. No actual Admin assignment or permission escalation was demonstrated.
reproSteps: As an administrator, create a disposable custom role with a limited permission set and Assignable to Workspace Members enabled.
Assign the custom role to a secondary member and confirm that the member’s Permissions tab displays it.
Open that role’s Settings, disable Assignable to Workspace Members, save, and reload to confirm the setting persisted.
Open the assigned member’s Permissions tab and observe that the Role selector now displays Admin or the first remaining eligible role instead of the actual custom role.
Compare the displayed permission set and Open in Roles target, or begin reassignment and inspect its confirmation, to verify that the original custom role remains assigned.
Re-enable member applicability and reopen the member’s Permissions tab; the correct role name returns.

bugs.name: API-key editor displays an unrelated role after API-key applicability is disabled
bugs.summary: Disabling API-key applicability on an already assigned custom role makes the API-key editor display a different role, while the saved role assignment remains unchanged.
bugs.expected: The API-key editor displays the key’s actual assigned role even when that role is no longer eligible for new API-key assignments.
bugs.actual: After Assignable to API Keys is disabled and saved on the assigned role, the key editor displays the first remaining eligible role, such as Admin or an unrelated custom role. The API-key list and saved role response retain the original assignment. Reload and a fresh session preserve the mismatch; re-enabling applicability restores the correct display. No actual role reassignment or change to effective API permissions was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Create a disposable custom role with Assignable to API Keys enabled.
Create a disposable API key assigned to that role and verify its role in both the key list and editor.
Open the assigned role’s Settings, disable Assignable to API Keys, and save.
Reopen the same key editor without reassigning the key and observe that its Role selector displays a different eligible role.
Reload or reopen in a fresh session and compare the incorrect editor value with the original assignment retained in the API-key list.
Re-enable API-key applicability on the original role and confirm that the editor displays the correct role again.

bugs.name: Re-enabling an AI tool trigger persists an empty parameter schema
bugs.summary: Disabling and re-enabling an AI tool trigger replaces its inferred parameter schema with an empty schema despite unchanged typed function code.
bugs.expected: Re-enabling an AI tool trigger retains or reconstructs its parameter schema from the unchanged function signature.
bugs.actual: A tool that previously listed typed parameters a and b shows No parameters after its AI tool trigger is disabled and re-enabled. The saved input schema has empty properties and generated sample input becomes {}. Reload preserves the empty schema. Editing the source, even adding whitespace, re-infers and restores the parameters. Actual AI invocation and downstream workflow behavior were not tested.
reproSteps: Open Settings > AI > Tools and create a disposable tool.

In its Editor, use a function with typed numeric parameters, such as export const main = async (params: { a: number; b: number }): Promise<object> => { return { sum: params.a + params.b }; }; and allow the edit to save.
Open Triggers, enable the AI tool trigger if needed, and confirm that parameters a and b are listed and generated sample input includes both.
Disable the AI tool trigger, allow the change to save, then re-enable it without changing the function code. Returning to the list and reopening the tool before re-enabling also reproduces.
Observe No parameters and generated sample input {}. Reload and confirm that the empty parameter schema persists.
As a control, edit the function source by adding whitespace and allow it to save; the parameter rows return.

bugs.name: Relations Type sorting does not sort the displayed relationship types
bugs.summary: The Type heading in an object’s Relations table changes its sorting arrow without sorting the displayed Has many and Belongs to one relationship types.
bugs.expected: Sorting the Relations table by Type groups the displayed relationship cardinalities consistently, with ascending and descending directions reversing their order.
bugs.actual: On mixed ordinary relations, clicking Type in either direction reverses the arrow but leaves Has many and Belongs to one rows interleaved in the same order. Reload and repeated clicks reproduce. The sorter compares the generic field kind RELATION shared by those rows instead of their displayed cardinality. Relations Name sorting and the neighboring Fields Data type sorting work; no relation-data corruption was observed.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Data model and select a disposable object with at least four ordinary relation fields alternating between Has many and Belongs to one. Create such fields if necessary.
Open the object’s Fields tab and locate the Relations table.
Click the Type heading to select one sorting direction and inspect the order of the displayed relationship types.
Click Type again to reverse direction and observe that the same mixed order remains despite the reversed arrow.
Reload and repeat both Type directions. As controls, sort Relations by Name and the neighboring Fields table by Data type; those controls reorder rows.

bugs.name: Removing a sidebar folder routes an adjacent external link on the app origin
bugs.summary: Removing a saved sidebar folder can automatically select an adjacent external link and route its path on Twenty’s own origin, opening a Page Not Found screen.
bugs.expected: Removing a sidebar folder leaves usable app content. If the next selected item is an external link, its configured origin is preserved and it is handled as an external destination.
bugs.actual: When the next selected sibling is an external link, removing the folder navigates to that link’s path, query and fragment on Twenty’s origin and displays Off the beaten path / Page Not Found. The saved link URL retains its external origin, and ordinary link clicks open the full external URL correctly in a new tab. Back to content recovers usable content and preserves the layout draft; no permanent data loss or runtime crash was established.
reproSteps: In Settings > Layout > Customize, create a disposable external link such as https://example.org/qa-layout?q=one#two and an empty folder immediately after it. Place the folder last among its siblings so removal selects the preceding link; save the layout.
Reenter customization, select the saved empty folder, and choose Remove from sidebar.
Observe that Twenty navigates to its own origin at /qa-layout?q=one#two and shows its Page Not Found screen instead of handling the configured external origin.
Use Back to content to recover and confirm that the layout draft remains available and the link editor still contains the full external URL.

As controls, use a normal external-link click and verify the full external destination opens, and remove a folder whose selected sibling is an internal object page to verify usable internal navigation.

bugs.name: Go to Domains Settings opens an empty settings page

bugs.summary: After desktop-to-tablet resizing, eligible pinned Company actions disappear from both toolbar and default command menu until search or reload.
bugs.expected: The initial command menu exposes eligible actions hidden from the toolbar at the same viewport width regardless of resize history.
bugs.actual: Both judges reproduced twice with fresh selected Companies: resizing to 768px hid Export and other pinned actions from the toolbar and empty-search menu while selection remained. Searching Export found it, and Codex downloaded a CSV. Reload at the same width restored the initial menu. Company record headers also reproduced.
reproSteps: As an administrator, pin and save Export Company for selected Companies through layout action customization.
At desktop width, select a disposable Company and confirm Export is available in the toolbar.
Resize to 768px and open the command menu with an empty search, preserving the selected row. Observe Export and the other formerly inline pinned commands are absent.
Search Export in the same menu and confirm it appears and can download CSV.
Reload at the same width, reselect the same Company, and confirm the empty-search menu now contains its pinned actions. Repeat with a fresh Company or full Company record page.
bugs.sourceCause: Mobile unmounts the pinned toolbar measurement producer, but shared inline-layout state retains desktop widths. The default menu incorrectly excludes actions it believes remain inline.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo report plus independent Claude Code and Codex browser reproductions and source audits, coordinator citation checks, and user acceptance.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: GUI-only: the demonstrated display or navigation state is wrong; no failed supported operation or saved-data loss was established.
analysis: Both judges recommend P/1; the original complete-unreachability claim is narrowed because search finds and executes the action.
The coordinator checked toolbar gates, retained measurements, default-menu filtering, selection eligibility and latest removal of the mechanism.
The helper’s zero-width return is not the fresh-mobile fallback: hasKnownPinnedInlineLayout=false separately makes the menu include pinned actions. This corrects Claude’s incidental explanation.

N66 reproduces the same measurement cause in the workflow editor; this approved related entry covers selected Companies and Company record headers. N52 is a distinct cross-browser metadata-cache trigger.
limitations: Search is a working recovery, and the CSV download completed; CSV contents were not audited.
No saved pin loss, selection loss or export execution failure is claimed.
Latest was source-inspected only.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers selected Companies list rows and Company record headers after desktop-to-tablet resize. workflows-N66 covers pinned Test/Deactivate/See Runs in a workflow editor. The stale layout-measurement cause is shared; match the page and commands. settings-data-model-N52 instead involves cross-browser metadata caching after saved pin updates.

bugs.name: Role detail reload ignores its Assignment or Settings URL fragment
bugs.summary: Reloading a role tab keeps its Assignment or Settings fragment in the URL but displays Permissions instead.
bugs.expected: A role detail link with a valid tab fragment opens that tab and its corresponding content after reload.
bugs.actual: Both judges reproduced repeated fresh-role reloads retaining #assignment while Permissions became selected with matching Permissions content. Built-in Admin and Settings-tab variations also reproduced. Reopening Assignment recovered; the sibling Members Roles tab preserved its selection normally.
reproSteps: As an administrator, create and save a disposable role, open its Assignment tab, and confirm Assigned Members is displayed with #assignment in the address.
Reload the page and allow loading to settle.
Observe that the address still ends in #assignment while Permissions is selected and its object/settings permission controls appear.
Click Assignment again and confirm it opens correctly. Repeat with another saved role or its Settings fragment.
As a control, open Members > Roles and reload; its valid #roles fragment and displayed tab remain consistent.
bugs.sourceCause: The role initialization effect writes Permissions after role loading, competing with URL-driven tab selection. The exact effect scheduling is inferred; the settled tab/address mismatch is observed.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo report plus independent Claude Code and Codex browser reproductions and source audits, coordinator citation checks, and user acceptance.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: GUI-only: the demonstrated display or navigation state is wrong; no failed supported operation or saved-data loss was established.
analysis: Claude recommends P/3 and Codex P/1. The user approved severity 1: no assignment changes, failed save or saved-role loss was demonstrated, and another click recovers.
The selected tab and content agree on Permissions. This excludes the rejected N51 claim that Settings remains highlighted while Permissions content appears.

The coordinator checked all citations and corrected an overlong loading-effect range. Latest has both a Permissions initializer and rewritten fragment-priority selection, so latest runtime status is left unverified.
limitations: No saved assignment or role setting was lost.
Do not match the distinct unreproduced selected-tab/content mismatch rejected as N51.
Exact initialization-effect scheduling and latest runtime behavior were not established.

bugs.name: Clearing Profile Last Name provides no validation or save-status feedback
bugs.summary: The autosaving Profile name editor silently leaves a cleared required Last Name in the field without indicating that it will not save; reload restores the saved name.
bugs.expected: The editor should explain that a cleared required Last Name is invalid or otherwise indicate that the displayed empty draft is not saved.
bugs.actual: Clearing Last Name and blurring leaves a blank field with no validation message and sends no save request. Reload restores the old name. Valid nonempty edits autosave and persist, also without an explicit Saving/Saved indicator.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Profile with a saved nonempty Last Name.
Change Last Name to a different nonempty value, wait for autosave, and reload to confirm it persisted.
Clear Last Name and leave the field. Observe no required-field validation or indication that this draft is not saving.
Reload and observe the previous saved Last Name return. No saved name was erased.
bugs.sourceCause: NameFields suppresses autosave when either required name is empty, while its inputs render no validation state and its save path exposes no explicit saving or success feedback.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo report, Claude browser reproduction with controls, independent Claude/Codex source review, coordinator source checks, and user acceptance of narrowed feedback scope despite both rejection recommendations.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Missing validation/save-status feedback only; required-name enforcement and persistence of valid names work.
analysis: Claude reproduced the empty field, absent validation, absent request and saved-name restoration twice; valid nonempty controls persisted. Codex rejected at source/contract review without independently browser-reproducing.

Both judges rejected the original claim because name clearing is intentionally prohibited. The user accepted only the missing-feedback issue at severity 1 after clarification that valid saves also have no explicit status indicator.
The required-name guard intentionally prevents returning users to onboarding. This entry does not demand optional Last Name or treat preserving the saved name as data loss.

Rejected N07 and other required-name entries retain their functional interpretation; this narrower label covers the unexplained unsaved Last Name draft. Latest retains the guard and no-feedback integration; latest runtime was not tested.
limitations: No failure to save a valid nonempty name and no saved-data loss were observed.

Codex stopped at source/contract review; Claude supplied the browser reproduction. Absence of explicit feedback for successful saves was additionally checked in source, not a new dedicated browser trial.
Both judges originally recommended rejection; severity 1 and the feedback-only scope are the user decision. Do not generalize into a requirement that every autosaving field show a success toast.
Latest was inspected in source only.

bugs.name: Sorting Skills by Type crashes AI settings
bugs.summary: Sorting the AI Skills list by Type throws a Boolean localeCompare error and replaces the settings page content with an error screen.
bugs.expected: Clicking the supported Type sort header should reorder Skills while keeping the settings page usable.
bugs.actual: Clicking Type replaces the AI settings tabs and Skills list with Sorry, something went wrong and a Reload button. The Settings sidebar remains visible. Reload restores the list, and clicking Type crashes it again. Saved Skill content remains intact.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > AI > Skills in a workspace containing multiple Skills.
If needed, create a uniquely named custom Skill alongside the seeded Skills and save it.
Click the Name sort header and confirm the list remains usable; correct Name ordering is not required for this control.
Click the Type sort header and observe the settings page content replaced by the error screen.
Use Reload, reopen Skills if necessary, and click Type again to reproduce the crash.
bugs.sourceCause: The Skills Type column declares the Boolean isCustom field as string. The shared sorter calls localeCompare on its Boolean value without conversion, throwing during list rendering.

reviewEvidence.basis: Focused Mo reproduction, independent Codex and Claude browser/source verification, coordinator source checks, and explicit user acceptance.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The settings page content, including its tabs and Skills list, is replaced by the page error display; the surviving sidebar and reload recovery follow the existing severity-5 page-crash convention.
analysis: Codex reproduced four completed Type-sort crashes across repeated loads and two widths; Claude reproduced twice. Each created one demonstration Skill and otherwise used seeded Skills in the same workspace.
Name sorting remained usable as a crash control. Reload recovered the list, and Codex verified its saved Skill name, description and instructions survived.
The stored/API isCustom value is Boolean, its column metadata says string, and the comparator calls localeCompare. A TypeScript assertion does not convert the value.

Upstream commit 08738e93c1c8d2d6617265ad210b662e630863a7 explicitly identifies this Skills crash. The inspected newer snapshot replaces Type/isCustom with string App labels; no newer-runtime test was performed.
The Indexes Unique crash shares the comparator mismatch but has different column metadata and a separate Data model entry point; this entry covers Skills Type only.
limitations: Repeated trials used one workspace, not multiple independent workspaces.
No saved-data loss or permanent outage was observed; the Settings sidebar remains and reload recovers.
Empty or single-Skill workspaces, other roles and broader platform behavior were not established.
Claude standalone screenshot files were unavailable; its recorded video and browser/console evidence were retained.
The inspected newer source was not run.

bugs.name: Sorting Indexes by Unique crashes Data model settings
bugs.summary: Sorting the Companies Indexes table by Unique calls a string comparator on a Boolean and replaces Data model settings content with the page error display.
bugs.expected: Sorting indexes by the supported Unique column should reorder the table while keeping Data model settings usable.
bugs.actual: Clicking Unique replaces the breadcrumb, header, tabs and Indexes table with the page error display while the Settings sidebar remains visible. Reload restores the table. Type sorting works, and the same displayed index names and uniqueness flags remain after recovery.
reproSteps: As an administrator, open Settings > Data model > Companies.
Enable Advanced and open the Indexes section with multiple indexes.
Sort by Type and confirm the table remains usable.
Click Unique to sort the indexes and observe the settings content replaced by the error screen.
Reload, reopen Indexes and repeat the Unique sort to reproduce the crash.
bugs.sourceCause: Indexes metadata declares Boolean isUnique as string. The shared sorter calls localeCompare on the Boolean and throws during rendering.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers Settings > Data model > Indexes > Unique, using isUnique metadata. The related entry covers Settings > AI > Skills > Type, using isCustom metadata. Both reach the shared Boolean/string comparator mismatch through different table columns and entry points.

reviewEvidence.basis: Dedicated Mo reproduction, focused continuations of both independent Codex and Claude reviewer sessions, coordinator source checks and user acceptance as a related entry.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The page breadcrumb, header, tabs and Indexes table are replaced by the error display; the sidebar remains and reload recovers.
analysis: Both reviewers reproduced twice from clean Companies loads, with passing Type-sort controls before Unique failed. Claude also reproduced on People.
Both verified the same three displayed Companies indexes and uniqueness flags after recovery and restored Advanced off. No index or record mutation was performed.
The Boolean isUnique value is declared string in table metadata and reaches localeCompare without conversion. The newer inspected source retains this mismatch, without runtime verification.
Mo assigned its own LOW custom score; severity5 is the user-approved page-crash score independently recommended by both focused reviewers.
limitations: No data loss or permanent unavailability was observed; the displayed-index comparison was not a separate database-ID audit.
Other roles, devices, empty/single-index tables and ascending Unique sort were not tested.
A brief sidebar-navigation recovery observation was uninvestigated and excluded.
Newer source was inspected but not run.

bugs.name: Workspace-logo replacement returns an error after saving the new image
bugs.summary: Replacing an existing logo repeatedly on the same General settings page can save the latest image but return an error and retain the previous preview.
bugs.expected: A supported logo replacement should return success and show the saved image. Deleting the previous logo must use its current identity.
bugs.actual: From a reload-verified working logo, the first replacement succeeds. A subsequent replacement on the same mounted page returns an error and retains the prior preview, although later workspace reads and reload reveal the latest image was committed.
reproSteps: Save a small genuine workspace-logo image in Settings > General and reload to verify it persists.
Replace it with a distinct valid image and confirm success.
Without leaving General, replace it again with another distinct valid image.
Observe the generic error toast and retained previous preview.
Reload and observe the newest replacement, showing that it was saved despite the error response.
Controls: repeated replacements from an empty baseline work; saving another workspace setting between replacements prevents the tested failure.
bugs.sourceCause: The upload saves a new logoFileId without invalidating cached workspaceEntity, then deletes the old ID from that cache. A later replacement commits before deletion of the already-deleted cached ID throws; the frontend does not install a failed request result.

matchingGuidance.distinction: N01 covers a valid workspace logo disappearing on first reload. This entry requires replacing a reload-verified existing logo repeatedly on the same General page and receiving an error after the latest replacement committed.

reviewEvidence.basis: Focused Mo reproduction, independently investigated server behavior from the original Codex/Claude review sessions, focused Codex valid-only follow-up, coordinator source checks and explicit related-entry acceptance.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Supported replacement returns an error after committing, leaving the displayed logo inconsistent with saved state.
analysis: Codex reproduced two complete valid-only sequences; independent Claude investigation found the same stale-ID deletion mechanism. Focused Mo repeated the existing-logo sequence twice.
Error toasts were observed; the initial Claude no-feedback claim is excluded. The stale prior ID comes from the server workspace cache, not an established client-supplied old ID.
Empty-baseline consecutive uploads worked, and a workspace-setting save between replacements prevented failure. No universal second-upload failure or fixed cache-expiry duration is claimed.
The inspected newer source reads the previous ID under a row lock, binds the replacement transactionally and invalidates the cache; that runtime was not tested.
limitations: Uses the already-completed independent original reviewer sessions; no additional standalone judge sessions are implied.
Cache expiry, concurrent uploads, other roles and onboarding were not browser-verified.
The tested files were small genuine images; oversized/invalid-file claims are outside this entry.
Newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: First profile-picture upload disables Abort while the request is pending
bugs.summary: With no existing profile picture, an oversized genuine PNG can leave an upload pending while its offered Abort action is disabled.
bugs.expected: An offered Abort control should cancel an active first profile-picture upload regardless of whether a prior picture exists.
bugs.actual: Approximately12.6MB genuine PNG uploads stayed pending for roughly96–130+seconds with Abort disabled when the profile had no picture. With an existing valid picture, Abort remained enabled and canceled the upload while retaining the old picture.
reproSteps: Use a disposable administrator profile with no existing picture and open Settings > Profile.
Upload a genuine PNG of approximately12.6MB.
While the upload remains pending, observe that the offered Abort action is disabled and cannot cancel the request.
Recover by reloading or clicking the picture tile and selecting a small valid image.
Control: with an existing valid profile picture, start an oversized upload and click the enabled Abort action; it cancels and retains the previous picture.
bugs.sourceCause: ImageInput disables Abort whenever pictureURI is empty, including an active upload before any first picture exists. The request cancellation handler exists but cannot be reached through the disabled control.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo report, independent Codex/Claude browser and source verification, coordinator source checks and user acceptance of the narrowed cancellation defect.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The cancellation action cannot be used during a pending first upload.
analysis: Each reviewer reproduced twice with fresh genuine approximately12.59MB PNGs, observing pending states beyond90seconds.
Small valid images succeed. Existing-picture Abort cancels and retains the old image. The picture tile can still select a small replacement and reload recovers.
The original complete-dead-end claim is excluded. Remove being disabled without a picture is expected and is not this defect.
Newer source removes the empty-picture Abort disabling condition and includes a first-upload Abort interaction check; newer runtime was not tested.
limitations: Pending observations are bounded, not proof requests never settle or a universal file-size threshold.
The full fixture server/proxy cause of the delayed rejection was not traced; reduced dependency experiments do not establish it.
No saved-picture or record-data loss was observed.
Other roles, devices and all upload callers were not established; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Saved Skill Instructions autosave remounts the editor and interrupts editing
bugs.summary: Autosaving changed Instructions in a saved Skill remounts its editor, closing fullscreen and formatting menus and losing focus.
bugs.expected: Autosaving Instructions should preserve the active editor, fullscreen state, focus and offered formatting menu so editing can continue.
bugs.actual: After editing expanded Instructions and pausing for autosave, the editor returns inline and loses focus. Continued typing without refocusing enters nothing. A slash-formatting menu also disappears after a changed value saves. Text entered before the remount persists through reload.
reproSteps: Create and save a uniquely named Skill with Instructions, then reopen it.
Expand Instructions, edit its content, and pause for autosave.
Observe the expanded editor close without a close action and lose focus. Attempt ordinary continued typing without refocusing; it enters nothing.
Reload and verify the text entered before the reset persisted.
Formatting variation: in a saved Skill, change Instructions and open the slash-command menu. Let the changed content autosave before choosing an option; the editor remounts and the menu disappears.
Controls: open saved Instructions without editing, or edit Instructions in an unsaved new-Skill form; the editor stays expanded. Sustained typing delays the reset until the debounce fires.
bugs.sourceCause: The frontend uses originalFormValues.content as the editor React key. Successful autosave updates that content and remounts the editor, resetting local fullscreen, focus and menu state.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo evidence, independent Codex/Claude browser and source reviews, separately verified formatting-menu variation, coordinator source checks and user acceptance of the Skills scope.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Successful autosave interrupts supported editing by closing fullscreen, dropping focus and dismissing the formatting menu.
analysis: Each reviewer reproduced on two fresh saved Skills. Separate independent reviewers confirmed the same remount dismisses the offered slash-formatting menu after changed content saves.
The backend stores entered content correctly. Later attempted characters never enter the unfocused editor; no erased saved instructions or persisted-keystroke loss is claimed.
Unsaved creation, unchanged saved content and no-change/arrow-key controls retain the editor. Identical-value edits skip saving and retain the menu.

Maintainer commit489118f25b44af148937450cc8678b5093200243 removes the autosave-dependent Skill editor key. Inspected newer source uses seeded content without that changing key; runtime correction was not tested.
Workspace Instructions also reproduced as a sibling, but this label covers the approved Skills entry point and its formatting-menu variation.
limitations: No saved-instruction loss was observed.
Other roles and all rich-text callers were not established.
Exact Claude save timing in the original fullscreen review was inferred from debounce/source and persisted content; the separate formatting review captured a successful update response and remount.
Newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Double-clicking Save creates two API keys for one completed creation form
bugs.summary: Rapid repeated submission of one valid API-key creation form creates multiple distinct persisted keys.
bugs.expected: A rapid double-click submitting one creation form should create one key, or block the repeated submission while creation is in progress.
bugs.actual: Rapid double-clicking Save creates two saved API-key records with separate IDs and detail URLs. Both remain after reload. Pressing Enter twice also reproduces.
reproSteps: Open Settings → MCP & APIs → API and choose Create API key.
Enter a unique valid name, select a role and expiration.
Rapidly double-click Save once, then wait for creation to complete.
Return to the API-key list and reload. Observe two persisted records for the single completed form; open each detail page to confirm separate IDs.
Control: submit a fresh form with one click; exactly one key is created.
bugs.sourceCause: The creation form has no in-flight guard or pending disabled/loading state. Save and Enter can reenter the asynchronous creation handler, and each invocation inserts a separate key.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo evidence, independent Codex and Claude browser/source reviews, coordinator source verification and user approval.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: One completed form unintentionally creates extra persisted API keys.
analysis: Both reviewers reproduced multiple times. Separate record IDs and detail URLs persisted after reload, excluding transient duplicate rendering.
Codex tested Admin and a custom assigned role with different expiration settings. Claude also reproduced with Enter twice and captured two creation and two token-generation requests.
Single-click creation controls each created one key. Double-click regeneration confirmation and sibling Webhook creation controls did not duplicate records.
Duplicate names are allowed; this label concerns repeated UI submission, not a server-side name uniqueness or API idempotency requirement.
Inspected newer source retains the missing guard; newer runtime was not tested. A remote automation-branch proposal is unmerged and unvalidated and does not establish maintainer intent.
limitations: Credential exposure, actual token use and downstream integration effects were not established.
Other signed-in actor roles were not tested.
Newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Skills Name sorting does not alphabetize the displayed skill names
bugs.summary: Skills Name sorting orders hidden API names rather than the displayed Skill labels.
bugs.expected: Ascending and descending Name sorting should alphabetize the displayed Skill names.
bugs.actual: Built-in Word Documents and Excel & Spreadsheets sort by docx and xlsx. Changing only a custom Skill API name changes its visible sort position despite an unchanged display name.
reproSteps: Open Settings → AI → Skills with the built-in Skills present.
Click Name to inspect ascending and descending order; compare Word Documents and Excel & Spreadsheets with the displayed labels around them.
Create two uniquely named Skills whose display names and API names initially sort in the same order. Confirm Name sorting orders them correctly.
Change only the alphabetically earlier Skill API name to one sorting after the second Skill. Observe its unchanged display name now sorts incorrectly in both directions, including after reload.
bugs.sourceCause: The Name column displays label but configures the client sorter to use name, the hidden API identifier, overriding the server label ordering.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo evidence, independent Codex and Claude browser/source reviews, checked maintainer correction and user approval.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The supported Name sorting function orders a different property from the names presented to users.
analysis: Both reviewers reproduced the built-in docx/xlsx mismatch and independently created an affected Skill plus a passing control.
Codex changed only an API name and verified both directions, reload and two widths. Claude independently confirmed both directions and reload/search behavior.

Maintainer commit 08738e93c1c8d2d6617265ad210b662e630863a7 explicitly identifies the mismatch and changes sorting to label. Inspected newer source includes the correction and a displayed-label sorting test; newer runtime and tests were not run.

The accepted Skills Type crash uses Boolean values with an incorrect string comparator; this entry concerns the Name column selecting the wrong string property. Relations Type sorting is in a separate table with a separate metadata constant.
limitations: No crash or saved-data loss occurred in Name sorting.
Each reviewer created one affected Skill and a passing control, rather than two independently affected fresh setups.
Other roles and newer runtime were not tested.

bugs.name: Role object-rule wizard discards pending global restrictions after member assignment
bugs.summary: After same-session role assignment, entering the object-rule wizard overwrites pending global permission restrictions, so saving retains the old globals instead of the intended restrictions.
bugs.expected: Opening an object-specific permission wizard should preserve pending global permission changes made in the same role edit session.
bugs.actual: Assigning a member to a fresh role without reload, unchecking All Objects and entering Add rule → Companies resets four pending false globals before Finish. Saving an object-specific Edit denial persists only that denial while the old true global values remain.
reproSteps: Create a fresh role and assign an existing member to it in the same session. Do not reload.
In Permissions, uncheck All Objects so the global permission restrictions are pending.
Open Add rule → Companies and observe the pending global restrictions revert before closing or finishing the wizard.
Deny Companies Edit, finish the wizard and save the role. Reload and observe that only the object denial persisted while the intended global restrictions did not.
Controls: repeat with a fresh unassigned role, or reload after member assignment before editing permissions; pending restrictions remain intact.
Restore any demonstration member to its original role after testing.
bugs.sourceCause: Immediate assignment stores a different member representation in role state. Network-only GetRoles on wizard mounts sees a deep difference and overwrites the entire dirty draft, discarding pending global restrictions. The resets are observed; precise callback ordering is inferred.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo candidate, independent Codex follow-up and Claude browser/source verification, coordinator checks and user acceptance.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Ordinary in-app configuration navigation discards pending permission restrictions and saves a configuration different from the intended changes.
analysis: Each reviewer reproduced on two fresh roles after same-session member assignment. Fresh unassigned and assigned-then-reloaded controls preserved pending edits. Codex’s original passing result missed this prerequisite and was revised after independent follow-up.
No already-saved false global was observed becoming true. Save sent only the object denial after pending global restrictions were lost; existing true server globals remained.
No exercised member-operation escalation or authorization bypass was established. Borrowed demonstration members were restored to their original Member role and verified after reload.

Inspected newer source removes the query’s draft write and preserves unsaved fields while synchronizing assignment collections. This supports a source-level correction without a newer-runtime or full release-fix guarantee.
The separate assignment-after-dirty-edit Save-disappearance observation lacks a second independent review and is excluded.
limitations: No already-saved restriction reversal or actual authorization bypass was demonstrated.
Precise callback ordering is inferred.
Original Mo historical causal chain was not independently replayed.
Other query consumers and newer runtime were not established.

bugs.name: Valid workspace image leaves a blank preview after an invalid upload
bugs.summary: After an invalid workspace-image upload, a later supported image saves but its preview stays blank in the mounted upload control.
bugs.expected: A successful valid image replacement should clear prior image-error state and display the newly saved workspace picture.
bugs.actual: After an invalid upload and a later supported valid upload, the valid image saves successfully but the same mounted picture control displays a blank placeholder. Navigating away and reopening settings restores the client preview.
reproSteps: Open Settings → General → Picture in a disposable workspace.
Upload an invalid image to put the preview into its error state.
Upload a supported genuine image and wait for the successful save.
Observe that the picture control still shows a blank placeholder despite the accepted valid replacement.

Navigate away and reopen settings to remount the control; observe the saved image preview recover. Do not rely on a first reload as the sole control because a separate workspace-cache issue can return stale references.
bugs.sourceCause: An invalid image sets the shared ImageInput client error flag. The same mounted control does not clear that flag after a subsequent supported image saves, leaving the successful replacement hidden behind the placeholder.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The existing reference covers profile-picture preview recovery after an invalid upload. This entry covers the workspace-logo entry point and successful later valid-image preview. Unsupported workspace-file acceptance and P2-8 server errors after replacement commit are distinct defects.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo evidence, independent Codex and Claude browser/source verification, coordinator checks and user acceptance of the narrowed client-preview related entry.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The supported valid image saves correctly while its preview remains blank. Codex and Claude both assign the narrowed preview defect severity 1; Claude’s overall severity 3 included a separately labeled server failure.
analysis: Both reviewers independently observed a successfully accepted valid workspace image with a blank preview after an invalid upload. Navigation/remount recovers the client display.
No loss of the successfully saved image is claimed. A separate workspace cache defect can interfere with first-reload recovery and is excluded from this client label.
P2-8 already covers valid-only replacement errors after committing a new image when an existing cached prior-file ID is stale. Its cause and accepted severity are not merged into this preview entry.

Accepted profile preview N33 shares the error-flag cause but uses a different upload entry point. Unsupported-file workspace upload coverage concerns accepting invalid content, not later preview recovery.
Inspected newer source keys the preview by source. This is source-level repair evidence only; newer runtime was not tested.
limitations: No saved-image loss is claimed.
First-reload recovery is unreliable because of a separately established server cache defect.
Other roles and widths were not established by both reviewers.
Newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Number format preview omits the requested trailing decimal zeros
bugs.summary: Plain Number fields omit trailing-zero padding despite their configured decimal count and explicit fixed-decimal helper example.
bugs.expected: A Number field configured for two decimal places should display trailing zeros consistently with the helper example, such as 2,000.00 and 1,234.50.
bugs.actual: The two-decimal preview displays 2,000 beside a helper example 1000.00. Saved records display 2000 as 2,000 and 1234.5 as 1,234.5. Fractional rounding still works: 1234.567 displays 1,234.57.
reproSteps: Create a fresh custom object with a plain Number field.
Set Number of decimals to two using the supported integer setting and compare the fixed-decimal helper with the preview. Observe missing trailing .00.
Save and reopen settings to confirm the decimal setting persisted.
Create records with values 2000, 1234.5 and 1234.567. Observe missing zero padding for the first two but correct two-decimal rounding for the last.
Controls: zero-decimal preview agrees with its helper and Short formatting displays the shortened form as configured.
bugs.sourceCause: The helper formats with toFixed, while the shared display formatter sets minimumFractionDigits to zero and uses the configured decimals only as maximumFractionDigits.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The existing Percentage reference and mo-60m-twenty-9 Currency/TWD reference share trailing-zero suppression in the formatter but cover their own field-type entry points. This entry covers plain Number configuration, preview and record display; correct fractional rounding is not classified as broken.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo candidate, independent Codex and Claude browser/source verification, coordinator checks and user acceptance as a severity-1 related entry.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The numeric values and saved settings are correct, but the displayed padding contradicts the explicit helper example.
analysis: Codex reproduced on two fresh custom objects with one, two and three decimals, typed and plus-button changes, saved/reopened settings and two widths. Claude reproduced two fields and input paths on one fresh object, including saved/reopened configuration.
Decimal precision is not wholly ignored: fractional values round correctly, zero-decimal and Short controls pass, and no stored values are lost.

The helper’s fixed-decimal example and display mismatch support the contract. Formatter history shows a change from matching minimum/maximum decimals to minimum zero, but the maintainer’s motive for record displays is not explicit.
Inspected newer source retains helper padding and zero minimum. Newer runtime was not tested.
Other billing, AI, aggregate and count callers sharing the formatter do not automatically have a fixed-padding requirement and are excluded.
limitations: No stored-value loss or failed field save occurred.
Claude used two fields on one fresh object rather than two independently saved objects.
Other roles and localization preferences were not established.
Newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Pinned Export View action disappears from the saving browser header after Layout customization
bugs.summary: A completed Export View pin save can leave the saving browser displaying and persistently caching the unpinned default despite the correct saved override.
bugs.expected: After successfully saving Export View as pinned, the saving browser should show the eligible header shortcut consistently with its stored customization.
bugs.actual: The shortcut intermittently disappears after saving while the server still reports the pin. Normal reload can retain the missing shortcut. Export remains available through command-menu search and executes; clearing browser IndexedDB and reloading restores the saved pin.
reproSteps: Open an eligible administrator index page and use Layout customization to pin Export View.
Save and allow the UI to settle. Observe whether the header shortcut disappears despite the completed saved pin. Labeled pins can reproduce; hiding the label is not required.
Reload and confirm the missing shortcut can persist while the server retains the pinned customization.
Search Export in the command menu and run it to confirm CSV export still works.
Clear this disposable browser’s IndexedDB and reload to fetch the effective saved pin and recover the shortcut.
